The Discourse on the Exercise of Sovereign Power at Will, etc.:
Is it the case that the Bodhisatta goes to a state of ruin for the sake of exercising sovereign power at will?
Yes, it is.
For the sake of exercising power according to his own will, the Bodhisatta goes to hell;
he goes to Sañjīva;
he goes to Kālasutta.
He goes to the Tāpana hell,
he goes to the Mahātāpana hell,
he goes to the Saṅghāta hell.
“He goes to the Roruva hell …pe… he goes to Avīci”?
One should not say so …pe….
“Does the Bodhisatta go to a state of ruin because of acting according to his own will for the sake of power?
— Yes.
“The Bodhisatta goes to a state of ruin because of acting according to his own will for the sake of power. — So it is said.

There is certainly no such sutta; yet, alas, you must not say:
“The Bodhisatta goes to a state of ruin for the sake of exercising power and fulfilling his desires.
[Is it true that] the Bodhisatta descends into the womb for the sake of exercising power and fulfilling his desires?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Then would the Bodhisatta, for the sake of exercising power according to his own will, be reborn in hell or be reborn in the animal realm?
You must not say so… [and so on]…
Is it true that the Bodhisatta descends into the womb for the sake of exercising sovereign power?
Yes. Is the Bodhisatta possessed of supernormal powers? Yes.
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is the Bodhisatta possessed of psychic power (iddhimā)? Yes.

The bodhisatta has cultivated the basis of psychic power consisting of concentration due to desire … [and so on] … the basis of psychic power consisting of concentration due to energy … [and so on] … the basis of psychic power consisting of concentration due to mind … [and so on].
Is it to be said that the basis of psychic power consisting of investigation has been developed? No, it should not be said so...
[and so on] ...Does the Bodhisatta enter the womb for the sake of exercising sovereign power according to his own will?
“Yes,” he said.
“Is there indeed a sutta that says: ‘The Bodhisatta descends into the womb for the sake of exercising sovereign power’?”
It is not so. If you say, "The Bodhisatta descends into the womb for the sake of exercising sovereign power," then such a sutta does not exist;
indeed, you should certainly not maintain that position.
“The Bodhisatta enters the womb for the sake of exercising sovereign power.
[If you say] the Bodhisatta performed ascetic practices for the sake of exercising sovereign power—yes, you say?—then [we ask]: Yes.
For the sake of exercising sovereign power, the Bodhisatta returned to the view that "the world is eternal," that "the world is not eternal," and so forth,
up to "the world is finite."
“The world is infinite,” … “the soul and the body are the same,” … “the soul is one thing and the body is another. …
“Does the Tathāgata exist after death?
… “Does the Tathāgata not exist after death?
… “Does the Tathāgata both exist and not exist after death? … [and so on] …
“Does one maintain that ‘the Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death’?
One should not say so… [and so on]… Did the Bodhisatta perform ascetic practices for the sake of exercising power and acting according to his own will?
“Yes,” he replied.
“Is there indeed a sutta that says: ‘The Bodhisatta performed austerities for the sake of exercising his sovereign will’?”
There is none.
If it were true that "the Bodhisatta performed ascetic practices for the sake of exercising sovereign power," there would be no such Sutta at all; indeed, you must not say that.
“The Bodhisatta performed ascetic practices for the sake of exercising sovereign power.

[If you say] “Yes,” then did the Bodhisatta perform self-mortification for the sake of exercising sovereign power, and did he designate another teacher? [If you say] “Yes,” then... [the rest of the argument follows].

Did the Bodhisatta, for the sake of exercising sovereign power, revert to the view that "the world is eternal" …pe… or revert to the view that "the Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death"?
One should certainly not say so …pe….
“Did the Bodhisatta, for the sake of exercising power at will, designate another teacher?”—
“Yes.”— “That ‘the Bodhisatta, for the sake of exercising power at will, designated another teacher’ [is true].”
Is there indeed such a sutta?
There is not.
For if it were the case that “the Bodhisatta, for the sake of exercising power and acting according to his own will, designated another teacher”—
There is indeed no such sutta, and certainly it should not be said:
"The Bodhisatta, for the sake of exercising power and acting according to his own will, designated another teacher.
The Discussion on Exercising Power and Acting According to One's Will is finished.
